title: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL — homeostatic regulation has a characterizable k-dependent stable band (0<k<1-alpha); fails outside it (8/8 falsifiers PASS from MEASURED trajectories)
question: Is homeostatic regulation (negative-feedback loop holding state x near setpoint x* despite a step perturbation) a real EMERGENT property with a characterizable stable feedback-gain band — STABLE inside, FAILING (oscillation/divergence/no-return) outside — rather than automatic for all k or for no k?
engine: discrete-time 2nd-order negative-feedback plant with inertia+actuator-delay, deterministic libm-free arithmetic, k-sweep with measured settling trajectories
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · ~1s wall · /Users/ghost/.hx/bin/hexa run · deterministic byte-identical

plant_model.velocity: v[t+1] = alpha * v[t] + u[t]   (inertia / actuator lag)
plant_model.analytic_stable_band_crosscheck: 0 < k < 1-alpha = 0.5 (Jury). Used ONLY as post-hoc cross-check, NEVER to decide PASS — PASS comes from measured |x-x*| trajectories.
plant_model.anti_tautology: x is NOT defined to equal x*; it is integrated from an independently-evolving velocity v. A divergent gain genuinely produces final|e|~1e47 (could have falsified F317.8). Not a snap-to-setpoint construction.

measured_boundary: Settling holds for every tested k in [0.05, 0.45] (inside 0<k<0.5) and fails for every tested k >= 0.50 and for k<0. The transition is sharp at the analytically-predicted k = 1-alpha = 0.5. The stable band is REAL and characterizable.
headline_finding: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL — homeostatic regulation is NOT automatic. There is a characterizable feedback-gain band 0<k<1-alpha (=0.5 at alpha=0.5): INSIDE it the loop returns x to within eps=0.05 of the setpoint (final|e| down to ~1e-15) after a step perturbation; OUTSIDE it the loop fails — k=0 never regulates (final|e|=10.0), the boundary k=0.5 is marginal (sustained oscillation, final|e|=10.23), k>=0.70 diverges (final|e|~1e16..1e47), and negative gain (positive feedback) diverges monotonically (~1e41). The measured boundary matches the Jury analytic prediction exactly. Both falsifier branches were live: regulation did NOT occur for ALL k (instability boundary exists), and DID occur for SOME k (it regulates) — so the 'characterizable stable band' claim survives.

criteria.C7_BAND_CHARACTERIZABLE: PASS (all k in [0.05,0.45] settle AND all k>=0.5 / k<0 do not — sharp boundary)

verdict_rationale: Falsifier was genuinely live: the claim would have failed if x returned to setpoint for ALL k>0 (no instability boundary) or for NO k (never regulates). Measurement shows neither — regulation occurs ONLY inside 0<k<0.5 and fails outside, a sharp characterizable boundary matching the Jury analytic band. Verdict is 🟢 (numerical/empirical simulation), NOT 🔵, because it is a measured dynamical result over a finite k-grid and finite horizon, not a symbolic closed-form identity.
honest_limits: L1 — toy 2nd-order plant (inertia+delay), not anima's full M-substrate. Maps the homeostasis AXIOM (negative feedback regulates within a stable gain band) onto a minimal model; not a claim about anima's exact M-controller implementation.

L2 — finite k-grid (9 points) and finite horizon (K=400). The boundary k=0.5 is inferred from grid edges + analytic Jury cross-check, not a continuum bisection. A denser sweep is a possible refinement, not required for the band-existence claim.
L3 — alpha=0.5 fixed. The band width is 1-alpha; alpha is a modeling choice. Different inertia shifts the boundary but does not remove it (band always nonempty for alpha<1).
L4 — final|e| ~1e-15 is float round-off floor (machine epsilon), i.e. exact convergence within numerical precision; eps=0.05 tolerance is far above it.
L5 — 🟢 not 🔵: empirical/numerical, SPECULATION-FENCED as a model of the homeostasis property, not anima's literal substrate controller.
